### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApproverType (symbol, a top-level const object), admin_rescue (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema), auto_approve (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via auto_approve (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`  _(via auto_approve (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ApproverType (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via admin_rescue (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema), auto_approve (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via ApprovalNodeConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via admin_rescue (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema), auto_approve (literal, a string literal in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2cf717ba4396f18b01c45126faf9d384d67e0ca3` — the merge of head `fc57c5652c4f1a1ed65f0d0126eba42246b5af45` into base `7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2cf717ba4396f18b01c45126faf9d384d67e0ca3 && git checkout 2cf717ba4396f18b01c45126faf9d384d67e0ca3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945 fc57c5652c4f1a1ed65f0d0126eba42246b5af45 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945 && git merge --no-ff fc57c5652c4f1a1ed65f0d0126eba42246b5af45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 审批节点设置的 23 条字段说明（Studio 流程节点检查器里显示的帮助文字）改成业务语言：第一句说这个设置对审批请求有什么作用，不再以 ADR 编号、内部字段名或枚举值开头；工程细节挪进代码注释，没有丢。
- **为什么改：** 18.3.0 RC 走查时管理员看到的帮助像工程文档（如 “ADR-0105 D9 —”、`submitter_id`、`admin_rescue`），看不懂该怎么设。
- **风险与回滚：** 只改说明文字，没有改任何键、类型、默认值或行为。回滚即 revert。
- **先看：** `packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/automation/approval-describe-business-words-27838.test.ts`，预期全绿（它扫描发布出去的 JSON Schema，旧文案下有 8 条红）。
- **需要你做的：** 无。不属于受管面，纯文案，由席位落地。HTTP 节点和审批节点在节点面板里的描述在别的包里，另开为 #28234。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT，可落地。

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · 2026-10-30T18:42Z

Head `fc57c5652c4f1a1ed65f0d0126eba42246b5af45`. Card #27838 (Part 1), claim 6528717388.

- **Shape:** draft to `main`, made by the relay; `Fixes #27838`; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (describe copy only). Changeset `@objectstack/spec` patch.
- **Contract review:** none owed. No key, type, default or accept set moves; the reference page is the regenerated describe text.
- **Diff read by the seat:** every changed `.describe()` opens with what the setting does to the request in business words (who can approve, the deadline and what happens when it passes, send-backs, record lock); the engineer detail (`onEmptyApprovers` pairing, ADR-0105 tokens) is kept in JSDoc. The new sweep test reads the published JSON Schema and was reverse-verified red on the old copy; the `excludeSubmitter` §5 pins moved with the copy. No translation bundle is fed by these describes (measured by the card thread).
- **Follow-ups filed:** #28234 (Part 2: the HTTP and approval node descriptor descriptions, outside `domain:spec`, with proposed wording).
- **Acceptance notes:** the Docs Drift Check lists `approvals.mdx`, `flows.mdx` and `common-patterns.mdx` for naming `admin_rescue` / `auto_approve`; no behaviour changed, so those pages stay. The stale quotation of the old escalation describe in a ui test header comment is noted, not filed.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head 41 success, 9 skipped, 0 red. `mergeable_state` clean. `check-governed-merges --branch`: NOT governed, 5 paths, +238/−97.
- **Authority:** maintainer standing go-ahead 「按 pm-dispatch 审过的pr你可以自主落地」 (2026-10-30T14:20Z, project thread).
- **Landing:** `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this act.

Success: Auto Label, Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter. Author `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note is owed. The reviewer is not the drafter (`session_01L9qibyR1YFTVfiVFt8svQ3`).

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is describe copy only. Every hunk in approval.zod.ts rewrites a `.describe()` or `.meta({ description })` string or adds a JSDoc / line comment; no key, type, `.default()`, `.min()`, enum member, `xRef` annotation, `superRefine` or refusal message moves. Checked line by line on the 23 strings the report names: ApproverType, approver value / resolveAs / group / organization, decision-output key / label (unchanged) / type / multiple / required, escalation enabled / timeoutHours / action / escalateTo / notifySubmitter, node approvers / excludeSubmitter / behavior / minApprovals / lockRecord / approvalStatusField / onEmptyApprovers / fallbackApprovers / decisionOutputs / escalation / maxRevisions.
- Against the card's Wanted (first sentence in business words, no decision id, internal field name or enum literal; engineer detail may stay in JSDoc): each new first sentence says what the setting does to the request; the keys and literals an author must write (`onEmptyApprovers`, `'auto_approve'`, `$root` / `$parent`, the escalateTo address forms, the CEL roots) follow in a later sentence; `submitter_id`, `admin_rescue`, the route names and the ADR-0105 D9 id moved into the JSDoc above the rows. The strings stay free of tracker ids (check-doc-authoring Rule 3 posture, which the ApproverType comment already records).
- Tests hold it in both directions: the new sweep walks every `description` in the published node JSON schema (path controls for a node key, an approver column, an escalation field and a typed output, so a top-level-only walk reds) and refuses six engineer shapes in the first sentence; the #25609 section 5 pins are re-cut so they no longer demand `submitter_id` or the "Segregation of duties" opening, still require `onEmptyApprovers` and `'auto_approve'` to be named, and now require that `submitter_id` is absent from the string. The PR's reverse verification (old describes restored, 8 failed / 36) matches that shape.
- Reference page regenerated from the describes; measured by the PR that no translation bundle carries these strings (ui tests hold their own fixtures), so no bundle move is owed.
- Changeset `@objectstack/spec` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: the right grade for copy that changes no accepted shape (the #28229 precedent).

### ② Semver level

patch. The authored protocol does not move: `check:authorable-surface` and `check:api-surface` are unchanged on the built dist per the PR body and the Governed Surface Queue Guard / Spec property liveness runs are green on the head; the JSON schema the Studio renders changes only in its `description` values.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `ui/**`, no governed path, no skill or ADR in the diff; the strings that were cut carry a decision id only in JSDoc now.
- Should-fix (not blocking, for the seat's follow-up cards): (a) Part 2, the node descriptor descriptions in service-automation `http-nodes.ts` and plugin-approvals `approval-node.ts`, is out of `domain:spec` and still reads as engineer copy; the report carries the proposed wording. (b) Two `ui/` leftovers the PR names: the Studio static fallback form `flow-node-config.ts` keeps its own hand-written approval help (used only when the engine publishes no `configSchema`) and now diverges in tone from the describes, and the header comment of `FlowNodeInspector.escalationOff-11660.test.tsx` quotes the old `enabled` describe as "the governing text". Both belong on the `domain:ui` half.
- Note: `onEmptyApprovers`'s first sentence lists all four outcomes in words and the second sentence restates the four literals; the sweep allows that by design (literals after the first stop), and the restatement is what an author typing the value needs.

### ④ Design judgment

The change holds against the surface it is read on and the scenario it is accepted against. The reader is the Studio flow inspector, which renders each property's `description` as the help line clamped to about two lines behind Learn more (PR #27832), so the first sentence is the whole message for most admins; putting the business meaning there and the engineer facts in JSDoc is the right split, and it keeps the describe as the single source for the generated reference page. The sweep pins the shape rather than the prose, so later copy edits stay free while the regression the card found (a decision id or storage column leading the help) cannot come back silently. The two rows the card singled out read correctly against their code: `excludeSubmitter` says the request goes to the administrators or the named backups and is never approved automatically, which is exactly what the ADR-0105 D9 / #25635 pairing refusal and the `admin_rescue` default enforce; `organization` says "another organization of the same group" and names the symbols after, matching `APPROVER_ORG_SYMBOLS` and the group-posture refusal recorded in its JSDoc. Scope discipline is right: Part 2 and the two `ui/` touches are left to their lanes with the wording recorded.
